doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-04-02

title: Trombonists: Sonny Henry and Ike Robinson
summary: De De names favorite trombonists Sonny Henry and Ike Robinson; Billie reports Ike is alive but sickly.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: I wondered about trombone players, if you had any favorite trombone players.
I like Henry's playing, Sonny Henry. I play, I have a big Ike, he died too.
Ike, he talks in Heavisand. Is that Robinson? Yeah, Ike Robinson, yeah, yeah, yeah. Ike, yeah. I work with him a lot.
I was thinking he was living, when did he die?

He said, I saw Ike's wife. Is he living? Yeah, she told me, yeah, Ike, listen. He's sickly, he's sickly. You remember? Wait, I tell you what happened. I went into Trimmy, to get something. I went to Trimmy to buy something for you. And I told you, I saw Ike's wife, told me she's still living in the same place. And I was sitting out on the step about a couple of weeks ago, she passed out there. Yeah, I think he's sick. I think he's sick. But she told me, no, Ike ain't dead. Ike ain't just a big and fat kid. I know, I know. I know, I know. He was so sickly there, you know. Yeah. But he didn't die, cause I asked her. She don't know him. No, he's still living in it. I don't know. He's still living in it, I don't know. He's passed, his wife passed here. And I was sitting outside there.
I don't know him at all. I must see him very soon, but I don't, I thought he was still living. I didn't know. I hope so. I didn't know, I hope so myself.

Yeah, I think he's still living, cause she told me, Ike, this is a big and fat, he don't get around. I believe she told me, my mistake, his eye is kind of bad on his sight. I believe that's what she told me.

What's the sign if I play nice, right? You play nice, right? You play nice, right? You play nice, right? You play nice, right? Yeah, sure. That boy played, that played somebody. That's the song that played sax. That's the song that played sax during the time I worked at St. Claude Street. That boy had his feet so bad there. Oh man, how you call me? Played trombone. I can't call his name. Trombone.
Is that the Cadillac or was it on St. Claude?
No, no, no. St. Claude, no. St. Claude. St. Bernard. St. Claude. St. Claude. St. Claude. St. Claude.
